newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares score record again, banks in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares score record again, banks in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher with the top-20 KFX index hitting a new all-time peak for the fourth consecutive day on Friday, with dealers seeing the positive market undertone continuing into next week.
"Maybe today's New York closure will put a damper on trade on Monday, inhibiting activity. Gains should continue but minor falls cannot be completely ruled out," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index ended the day 2.11 point up at a new record closing high of 177.76, while the KFX August future put on 2.70 point to close at 178.70 with 70 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
An acute lack of sellers in bank paper in a becalmed summer holiday market meant that bank shares noted solid gains.
Dealers said there was was no other apparent reason for the bank climbs, as an imbalance of buyers and sellers pushed up the price of the big three banks.
Den Danske Bank closed an impressive 23 crowns up at 710, with second-largest bank group Unidanmark finishing six crowns higher at 398 and third-biggest BG Bank ending 14 crowns more costly at 385.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.315 billion crowns.
